topic: The Physics of Pi: Why Colliding Blocks Calculate Circles
target_audience: High school physics students and undergraduate math enthusiasts

sections.title: The Mysterious Setup
lecture_lines: Imagine two blocks between a wall and an observer.
A massive block slides toward a smaller one.
We count every collision until they drift away.
animations: Fade in a white wall (#FFFFFF) and a small green block (#00FF00) sitting next to it.
A massive blue block (#0000FF) slides in from the right toward the small block.
Show the first collision between blocks and the wall, starting a '1' counter (#FFFF00).

sections.title: The Power of 100
lecture_lines: Mass ratios of 100 reveal a surprising pattern.
Ratio 1 to 1 produces 3 collisions.
Ratio 1 to 100 produces 31 collisions.
Ratio 1 to 10,000 produces 314 collisions.
These blocks are calculating the digits of Pi.
animations: Display 'Ratio 1:1' (#FFFFFF) and animate 3 rapid collisions between the blocks.
Display 'Ratio 1:100' (#FFFFFF) and show a counter (#FFFF00) reaching 31.
Display 'Ratio 1:10,000' (#FFFFFF) and show the counter (#FFFF00) reaching 314.
Highlight the sequence 3, 31, 314 in yellow (#FFFF00) and compare to Pi.
A magenta Pi symbol (#FF00FF) pulses and grows in the center of the screen.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: Two physical rules govern every single "click."
Conservation of energy keeps the total budget constant.
Momentum transfers between blocks during each impact.
animations: Display the Kinetic Energy equation: 1/2mv^2 + 1/2MV^2 = E in cyan (#00FFFF).
Display the Momentum equation: mv + MV = P in orange (#FF8000).
Flash both equations in white (#FFFFFF) during a simulated collision to indicate conservation.

sections.title: Mapping Physics to Geometry
lecture_lines: Let's map block velocities onto a coordinate graph.
Rescaled velocities must follow the energy conservation law.
This energy constraint forms a perfect circle.
Each collision represents a step along this arc.
Physics is transforming into a geometric puzzle.
animations: Draw a green circle (#00FF00) centered on a coordinate plane of velocities.
Place a red dot (#FF0000) on the circle to represent the blocks' current velocity state.
Jump the red dot to a new position on the circle, representing a block-to-block collision.
Draw a white line segment (#FFFFFF) connecting the previous and new positions on the circle.
Rapidly add more segments as collisions continue, tracing a path around the circle.

sections.title: Unfolding the Circle
lecture_lines: Increasing mass ratio makes each step much smaller.
More collisions are needed to traverse the circle.
The total count relates to the circle's circumference.
Pi emerges from the ratio of distance to diameter.
The number of steps reveals Pi's hidden digits.
animations: Highlight a small yellow arc segment (#FFFF00) representing the change from one collision.
Show the arc segment shrinking as the mass ratio M/m is increased.
Animate the entire green circle (#00FF00) unrolling into a straight white line (#FFFFFF).
Fill the straight line with these small arc segments to count how many fit.
The total count of segments morphs into the decimal digits of Pi (#FF00FF).

sections.title: Conclusion: The Hidden Harmony
lecture_lines: Colliding blocks hide a beautiful circular secret.
Linear physics and circular geometry are deeply connected.
Pi appears even where no physical circles exist.
animations: Overlay the colliding blocks and the velocity circle, then merge them into Pi (#FF00FF).
Display the text 'Hidden Geometry' (#FFFFFF) and scale it up for emphasis.
Fade all elements to black, leaving only a glowing magenta Pi symbol (#FF00FF).
